The Tab key visits every element with a positive `tabIndex` first, from the lowest number to the highest, and only then the rest of the page. Focus jumps around in an order that doesn't match what's on the screen, and every new control means renumbering the others.

Use `0` to put an element in the tab order at its place in the document, and `-1` to make it focusable from code only. To change the order, move the elements.

A value that's only known at run time, such as `tabIndex={order}`, isn't checked.

`--fix-dangerously` changes the value to `"0"`. `--fix` doesn't, because that changes the tab order.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"jsx-a11y/tabindex-no-positive" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```jsx
const form = (
  <form>
    <input name="email" tabIndex={2} />
    <input name="name" tabIndex="1" />
  </form>
);
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const form = (
  <form>
    <input name="name" />
    <input name="email" />
    <div role="button" tabIndex={0} />
    <h2 tabIndex={-1}>Done</h2>
  </form>
);
```
